title_options: Agent Memory Tracing: OpenTelemetry Spans for Write, Retrieve and Evict
See Why Agent Memory Fails: One OpenTelemetry Span per Write, Read and Eviction
OpenTelemetry Memory Spans: Instrument create_memory, search_memory and delete_memory
presentation.title_rationale: It frontloads the topic (agent memory tracing) and the concrete reader problem (write, retrieve and evict are the three paths whose failure looks identical), and promises the one benefit the article delivers: the spans and attributes that separate them. The spec name and the Development status sit in the subtitle, not the title, because a reader searching for why recall is wrong needs the problem first.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover shows the three traces from the published dump as a waterfall: a create_memory batch, two search_memory spans for the same query returning different values with no write span between them, and a delete_memory with an eviction reason. It explains the article's central claim visually - a changing read with no write span is what a stale answer looks like in a trace - and it is drawn only from spans.json, with a footer stating it is span shape, not a measurement.
